subheading: CLINICAL FEATURES OF GUINEA WORM DISEASE (DRACUNCULIASIS)
subheading_corrected: CLINICAL FEATURES OF GUINEA WORM DISEASE (DRACUNCULIASIS)
text:
Clinical Features
- As the worm approaches the surface it may be felt as a cordlike thickening
- It forms an indurated cutaneous papule
- Several hours before the head appears at the skin surface there is (at the
point of emergence)
- Local erythema
- Burning sensation
- Pruritus
- Tenderness
- Soon after, the papule blisters and a painful ulcer develops, usually on the
leg
- Ulcer may occur on other parts of the body e.g. the genitalia, buttocks, or
arms
